• The project focuses on **habitat conservation**, **prey base management**, and mitigating **man-animal conflict** across **eight** identified sanctuaries.
 
• Other major leopard habitats in the state include **Jhalana Leopard Reserve** in **Jaipur** and the **Jawai** region in **Pali**.
 
 
 
• **Leopard Characteristics and Features:**
 
 
• The leopard (**Panthera pardus**) is the smallest of the **big cats** but is known for its extreme **agility** and **nocturnal** hunting habits.
 
• They are highly **adaptable** and can survive in diverse climates, ranging from **tropical rainforests** to **arid rocky terrains** like the **Aravalli Range**.
 
• Leopards are **solitary** animals, and their **rosettes** (spots) serve as excellent camouflage in the scrub forests of **Rajasthan**.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Context:**
 
 
• The **Aravalli Hills** are among the world's oldest **fold mountains**, stretching across **Gujarat**, **Rajasthan**, and **Haryana**.
 
• The **rocky outcrops** and **cave systems** in the **Udaipur** segment of the Aravallis provide natural shelters for leopards, making it a **prime location** for their survival.

• Leopards are protected under **Schedule I** of the Indian **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**, granting them the highest level of legal protection in the **country**.
 
• On the **IUCN Red List** of Threatened Species, the leopard is categorized as **Vulnerable** due to habitat loss and **illegal wildlife trade**.
 
 
 
• **Population Data:**
 
 
• According to the **Status of Leopards in India** report (latest cycles), India has seen a significant percentage increase in its leopard population. **Madhya Pradesh** generally holds the highest number, but **Rajasthan** excels in **density per square kilometer** in specific hilly pockets like **Udaipur**.

• The 'Leopard Capital' tag facilitates the development of **Leopard Safaris**, similar to the **Jhalana** model, providing **employment** opportunities for local youth in **Udaipur**.

• **Usain Bolt**, the **Jamaican** sprinting legend, was named a **Guinness World Records ICON** in **June 2025** (marking a milestone anniversary of his peak achievements) for his unprecedented dominance and lasting impact on **Track and Field**. *Hence, option B is correct.*
 
• He is the world record holder in the **100 metres**, **200 metres**, and the **4 × 100 metres relay**, making him the **fastest man in history**. His 100m record of **9.58 seconds** and 200m record of **19.19 seconds** were both set at the **2009 World Athletics Championships** in **Berlin**, **Germany**.
 
• **Usain Bolt** has secured a total of **8 Olympic gold medals** and is the only sprinter to win the **Olympic 100m and 200m titles** at three consecutive **Olympics** (**Beijing 2008**, **London 2012**, and **Rio 2016**).
 
• The title of **Guinness World Records ICON** is reserved for individuals whose achievements are so significant that they redefine their field; Bolt holds the record for the **most IAAF World Championship gold medals** won by a male athlete (**11 gold medals**).
 
• Other athletes mentioned like **Justin Gatlin**, **Carl Lewis**, and **Michael Johnson** are legends in their own right, but they do not hold the specific **ICON** status designated for this timeframe or the current world records in the primary sprint categories. *Hence, options A, C, and D are incorrect.*

__
 
• The **inaugural Everest Climbers’ Summit** on climate change was held in **Kathmandu, Nepal**, in **May 2025**. The summit was organized to bring together world-renowned mountaineers to highlight the alarming rate of **glacier melt** in the **Himalayas**.
 
• The event was timed to coincide with the **International Year of Glaciers' Preservation** (**2025**), as declared by the **United Nations General Assembly**. This initiative seeks to raise global awareness about the vulnerability of mountain ecosystems.
 
• The summit served as a platform for climbers who have summited **Mount Everest** multiple times to share their **firsthand observations** of environmental changes, such as the thinning of the **Khumbu Glacier** and the increasing frequency of **avalanches**.
 
• A key objective of the **2025 Summit** in **Kathmandu** was to pressure the international community to meet the goals of the **Paris Agreement**, specifically aiming to limit global warming to **1.5°C** to save the "**Water Tower of Asia**."
 
• The **Government of Nepal**, through the **Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Civil Aviation**, led the initiative to ensure that the voices of those who know the mountains best are heard in global climate policy discussions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Climate Impact on the Third Pole:** The **Himalayan-Hindu Kush** region is often referred to as the **Third Pole** because it contains the largest ice reserves outside the polar regions. Recent data from **ICIMOD** (International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development) suggests that glaciers in this region could lose **30% to 80%** of their volume by the year **2100**.
 
• **The Khumbu Glacier:** This is the highest glacier in the world, located in the **Solukhumbu District** of **Nepal**. Studies have shown that the **South Col Glacier** on Everest has lost nearly **2 meters** of ice thickness annually in recent decades due to **anthropogenic climate change**.
 
• **Sagarmatha Sambaad:** This is a multi-stakeholder dialogue forum established by the **Government of Nepal** in **2019**. It focuses on global, regional, and national issues, with **climate change** being a primary theme for its inaugural sessions.
 
• **Historical Significance:** The summit also paid tribute to the **72nd anniversary** of the first successful ascent of **Mount Everest** by **Sir Edmund Hillary** and **Tenzing Norgay** in **1953**, emphasizing that the mountain they climbed is vastly different from the one climbers face today.

• **International Year of Glaciers' Preservation:** In **2022**, the **UN** passed a resolution, sponsored by **Tajikistan** and supported by **Nepal**, to declare **2025** as a year to focus on **glacier retreat** and its consequences for **sea-level rise** and **biodiversity**.
